title: Batch blob parameter transfer via TransferableTypedData
impact: Tests whether exp 234's accepted single-row blob-transfer win (wrap `Uint8List` params `>= 256 KB` in `TransferableTypedData` so their main->writer hop lands in malloc'd external memory instead of the GC heap) extends to the batch (`BatchRequest`/`executeBatch`) path, the direction's standing open question. **Rejected — reproduced regression, no size shows a win.** On a blob-heavy `executeBatch` (30 rows/batch, one blob each), the 256 KB lane — the exact size where single-row INSERT won -16% to -23% — is candidate-*slower* on 8/8 order-flipped legs, +7.6% to +18.1% (median ~+9.5%); 512 KB leans slower (7/8) and 1 MB is uniformly slightly slower, WAL-dominated. The mechanism inverts: exp 234's win came from many independent write round-trips whose per-send heap churn stalls the writer *mid-`sqlite3_step`*, a cost that compounds and that moving blobs off-heap removes. `executeBatch` already collapses N writes into ONE writer round-trip inside one transaction, so there is no scavenge-vs-writer-step interleaving to reclaim — leaving only the candidate's 30x `fromList` (malloc + finalizer + external-memory accounting) and 30x `materialize()` wrap tax against a baseline whose single graph-copy of all 30 blobs is a one-time transient the writer never races. Bounds exp 234's claim: the blob-transfer win is specific to per-round-trip churn, not GC-heap blobs in the abstract. Runtime reverted (`BatchRequest` stays on the direct copy); `blob_batch_write_ab.dart` harness kept as the durable gate; prototype preserved at `archive/exp-237`.
